title: review: S5: active skill routing for trusted builtin skills: selected compact skills are presented in the worker packet (Level 2), static exposure is switched off for Claude workers, recovery reads are measured; gated by [skills] mode and a safety refusal (v3)
spec:
Program brief .orchestrator/roadmap-skills.md P8 step 7, P10, P12 (skills part), P30 recovery (P37 stage 5). Depends on T-0913 (skill_router.select, [skills] mode, skill_selection rows, skills_selected in packet meta) and T-0894 (skills_used detection). Facts (Planner grep): Claude workers are launched by spawn.run_claude as `claude -p <prompt> --model ... --allowedTools ... [--disallowedTools ...]` with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account (spawn.py ~781-795); the CLI offers `--disable-slash-commands` ("Disable all skills") and `--plugin-dir`; worktrees carry the repo's committed .claude/skills symlinks, which is today's static exposure; skills with scripts are invoked through `bash skills/<role>/<name>/scripts/...`, which the allowlists already permit (Bash(bash skills/*)); Codex executors get implement-spec through AGENTS.md; skills_registry.render(id, 2) gives the compact body.
Do:
1. Presentation: when [skills] mode == "active", the worker packet gains a section "## skills" carrying, for each selected skill, a header line "### <id> (v<version>)" and its Level 2 rendering; the section sits after the role instructions and before the task contract sections; for Codex executors the same section goes into the execute packet (implement-spec always selected for executors, so Codex sees the compact body in the packet as well as via AGENTS.md). Ambiguous candidates are listed as one Level 0 line each under "### available on request" so a worker can Read skills/<id>/SKILL.md when it needs one.
2. Exposure: in active mode Claude workers are launched with `--disable-slash-commands` so the static .claude/skills descriptions no longer load; nothing in .claude/skills, the repo or the worktree changes. In shadow and off the launch is byte-identical to today (test asserts the argv).
3. Telemetry: skill_tokens_presented_l2 in packet meta and run context; the skill_selection decision row's selected = presented ids, mode = active; skills_used detection (S1b) extended: a Read of skills/<role>/<name>/SKILL.md by the worker, or a bash invocation of that skill's script, counts as a use; a use of a skill that was not presented counts as a skill_recovery (S3 metric).
4. Safety refusal: active is refused (falls back to shadow with one notify line) when skill_scorecard shows fewer than 30 shadow selection rows for the role over the last 7 days, or a skill_recovery_rate above [skills] max_recovery (new key, default 0.10) for that role. Planner role is never switched (the interactive Planner keeps its own skills).
5. docs/skill-intelligence/06-active-routing.md (≤60 lines): mechanism, the refusal rules, how to read the recovery rate, revert path ([skills] mode shadow restores static exposure on the next spawn).
Tests (unittest): tests/test_spawn.py::test_active_skills_section_carries_level2_of_selected_only, ::test_active_launch_adds_disable_slash_commands_and_shadow_does_not, ::test_active_refused_without_shadow_evidence_or_with_high_recovery, ::test_skill_use_detected_from_read_of_skill_file_and_script_invocation; tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_presented_tokens_and_recovery_from_active_rows. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally. Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-23 06:25) after spec review T-0930 (request_changes), binding on top of v1:
- Placement: the "## skills" section is the FIRST section of the packet body built by spawn._packet_body / review_packet (before objective), so it needs no prompt-template change; prompts/*.md stay out of scope. The packet header (packet_run_meta) records the section like any other (chars, tokens, hash).
- Budget: the skills section counts against the 4800-char packet budget and is protected like acceptance (never trimmed by the generic loop); it has its own cap: presented Level 2 text ≤ 2400 chars; when exceeded, the lowest-ranked non-mandatory selected skill is demoted to Level 1, then dropped, until it fits, and the demotion is recorded in the skill_selection row ("demoted": ids).
- Remove the stage-3 notify strings ("skill routing active is shadow-only until Stage 5") and their latch in spawn._skill_routing and executor._route_skills; active now means the behaviour in this spec, and the only remaining notify is the safety refusal message.
- Evidence for the refusal rule: add role to every skill_selection decision row (both call sites); skill_scorecard.selection_rows(root, role, since_s) counts shadow/active rows for that role from the decision log over the window; the refusal uses that function (fewer than 30 rows in 7 days) plus skill_scorecard's recovery rate for the role.
- Drop the Planner exemption sentence: no Planner launch site calls skill_router today (planner_shadow.py builds its own packets), so the rule is simply that only roles routed through spawn.run_worker and the Codex dispatch path are affected.
- Tests: tests/test_spawn.py::test_skills_section_is_first_packet_section_and_capped (a selected set whose Level 2 exceeds 2400 chars demotes the lowest non-mandatory skill to Level 1 and records it), tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_selection_rows_by_role_and_window.

SPEC v3 (2026-09-23 07:10) after spec review T-0937 (round 2; points folded in, further review waived by the Planner, verdict set to approve):
- Selection runs exactly once per worker dispatch, BEFORE the packet body is built: spawn.dispatch/run_worker and the Codex dispatch path call skill_router.select first and pass the result into packet()/review_packet() (new keyword `skills=`), and the same result feeds the decision row and the packet meta; no second select call after the body exists.
- All four skill_selection decision_log.record call sites (spawn._skill_exposure, spawn._skill_routing, executor._route_skills, executor's stage-1 static branch) carry `role` as a top-level row field (in addition to anything nested).
- Scope of active presentation: execute and review roles only (execute packet and review_packet). For scout, spec_review and challenge the router still runs and logs, but the decision row records mode "shadow" and presented = [] so selected == presented holds by construction for every row; scout_packet, spec_review_packet and the challenge render are untouched.
- The refusal rule's recovery rate is time-windowed: skill_scorecard.recovery_rate(root, role, since_s) derives it from decision_log outcome rows (skill_recovery outcomes / selection rows) within the same since_s window as selection_rows; build()'s all-time by_role value is not used for the refusal.
- New tests are methods on the existing SkillScorecardTests class in tests/test_skill_scorecard.py (test_selection_rows_by_role_and_window, test_presented_tokens_and_recovery_from_active_rows, test_recovery_rate_windowed); tests/test_spawn.py::test_selection_runs_once_before_packet_build asserts a single select call per dispatch with the section present in the packet.

comments.issue: decision_log.record() has no `role` parameter, so none of the four skill_selection call sites can put role at the row's top level as SPEC v3 requires ('All four skill_selection decision_log.record call sites carry role as a top-level row field'). spawn._skill_exposure nests it only in deterministic (spawn.py ~29-33); spawn._skill_routing and executor._route_skills nest it in extra (spawn.py ~311-315, executor.py ~113-119); executor.py's stage-1 static branch (~line 149) nests it in deterministic too. The row dict built in record() (decision_log.py:133-147) has no top-level 'role' key, so row['role'] is always None in production. skill_scorecard._selection_rows currently masks this with a 3-way OR fallback (row.get('role') or deterministic.role or extra.role), so today's refusal gate still counts correctly, but this is a real deviation from the binding spec that the acceptance tests don't catch (they mock decision_log.read_all with hand-built rows that already have role at top level, never exercising the real call sites). Any future consumer trusting the documented top-level contract will silently get None.
